name: Agentic AI UW
mission: Agentic AI UW is a community for learners, builders, generalists, entrepreneurs, and techno-optimists. We believe that the purpose of Engineering work is to create values and build useful products for people. Therefore, every year as a whole club, we attempt to build a revolutionary consumer-facing product with real users and real-world impact. Students who join our club will gain valuable knowledge and skills working with AI systems. They will gain experience working with a team of people on a large-scale project to prepare them to work in the industry. They will learn how to engineer products that are actually useful for people. Most importantly, they will gain lifelong connections with like-minded people who are also learners, builders, generalists, entrepreneurs, and techno-optimists. We also encourage our club members to utilize the connections they made in the club and build startups after graduation. Due to the entrepreneurial focus of our club project, we fully expect our club alumni to form multiple startups with great impact in the AI industry and beyond. However, one point to emphasize is that even with the club’s focus on building a consumer-facing product, the club itself will never become a precursor to a startup (more details in the “Projects” section). The club also aims to build strong connections with professors, labs, departments and other student organizations within the university. Outside of the university, our club aims to build connections with companies, government, investors and more. At the same time, we aim to keep our alumni community continually get involved with our college club. In this way, we hope to create a strong virtuous cycle between our club and other entities: a continuous transfer and flow of skills, funding, knowledge, and more.

mission: Alpha Sigma Phi is not interested in only becoming the fraternity of choice, for this perspective unnecessarily narrows our recruitment efforts to those inclined to go Greek. mission: EZ Bots is an organization dedicated to lowering the barriers to who can build, modify, deploy, and benefit from robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). Today, robotics and AI has advanced rapidly, yet access to capable robots remains constrained by cost, specialization, and technical complexity. Many robotic systems are designed around specific tasks and fixed physical forms, requiring different platforms or the purchase of a new robot for applications such as education, delivery, social interactions, accessibility, or collaborative work. At the same time, researchers developing new forms of human-robot interactions often have to integrate or build specialized hardware and software before they can translate an interaction concept into a deployable system. This fragmentation creates barriers to both using robots and creating them. These barriers disproportionately affect lower-income individuals, schools, communities and researchers with limited recourse, potentially widening existing disparities in access to emerging technologies. Our mission is to develop affordable, one-for-all modular robotics where both the body and intelligence can adapt to changing needs. A shared central intelligence can assemble and reconfigure its capabilities, while the physical system can be rebuilt through interchangeable components via self-assembly or human-assisted assembly. Instead of creating a new robot and intelligence for every application, the same ecosystem could rebuild both how it thinks, behaves and how it takes form for various domains such as education, delivery, social interactions, collaborative work, accessibility healthcare, and everyday assistance. For researchers, we aim to provide reusable physical modules and modular intelligence that reduce the resources required to transform an interaction concept into a deployable system. For everyday users, non-profits, and communities, we envision affordable robots that can evolve with their needs rather than requiring them to continually purchase new systems. Ultimately, EZ Bots seeks to democratize adaptable robotics by expanding who can build, modify, deploy and benefit from robotics and AI. At EZ Bots, we pursue this mission through an iterative process of collaborative design, prototyping, testing, and evaluation, with the ultimate goal of making adaptable robotics readily available to those who need it most. We envision a future where a robot is not defined by a single body, intelligence, or purpose, but can reconfigure what it is, how it thinks, and what it can do around the people it serves.
membershipBenefits: Learn hands-on engineering experience by designing, prototyping, testing, and troubleshooting real-world robotic applications. MAV MED engages with military-affiliated groups to promote a deeper understanding of military aspects and opportunities within medical education and career paths. MAV MED hosts educational sessions to advance medical knowledge, research, and the practice of medicine. The organization emphasizes mentorship, guidance, academic research, and support for military-connected medical students, while providing opportunities for exposure to military-related medicine. Members of MAV MED have a duty to uphold the organization’s core values and serve the community. name: Wisconsin Union Theater
mission: As the premier performing arts presenter at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, the Wisconsin Union Theater brings extraordinary music, dance, and theater to life while serving as a learning lab for student leaders. Through the Wisconsin Union Directorate, students gain hands-on experience in artistic curation, artist services, and event promotion with mentorship from professional staff. WUT also welcomes university departments, student organizations, and the greater Madison community, who rent our venues for performances, symposiums, graduations, and conferences. WUT also operates Campus Arts Ticketing, providing ticket sales and box office services for arts organizations and events across the UW–Madison campus community. The idea for a theater at the Wisconsin Union emerged before the 1920s, when University President Charles Van Hise and members of the Memorial Union Building Committee envisioned the arts as integral to campus life. Porter Butts helped turn that vision into reality, using his leadership, organizational, and fundraising abilities to establish what would become the Wisconsin Union Theater (WUT). Today, WUT’s mission is to present, promote, and cultivate a lifelong appreciation of the performing arts, especially among University of Wisconsin–Madison students. Its facilities include Shannon Hall, a 1,157-seat theater; the Play Circle, a flexible black box theater; and the Festival Room, a rehearsal and dance studio. These spaces feature professional sound and lighting systems, sprung stage floors, and exceptional acoustics. Through a student-led committee, WUT presents a season of music, dance, theater, festivals, and other performing arts experiences. Students gain hands-on experience in artistic programming, artist services, event promotion, and production while working alongside professional staff. WUT also serves as a gathering place for the campus and the greater Madison community, hosting graduations, lectures, conferences, and performances presented by university departments, registered student organizations, and community organizations. WUT operates Campus Arts Ticketing (CAT), providing ticketing services for the Wisconsin Union Theater and numerous campus and community arts organizations. CAT distributes approximately 100,000 tickets annually through permanent and satellite locations. The Wisconsin Union Theater strives to create an equitable, diverse, inclusive, and welcoming environment for staff, students, artists, performers, and audiences. Social justice informs its decision-making, workplace practices, programming, and activities, helping WUT respond to the needs and interests of the communities it serves while continuing its longstanding tradition of connecting students, campus, and the broader community through the performing arts.

name: Women's Club Basketball - University of Wisconsin-Madison
mission: Our mission is to provide female students with the opportunity to participate in competitive basketball throughout the school year. Through weekly practices and weekend tournaments, we wish to provide an outlet for students to develop their basketball skill sets while building relationships with teammates.

name: Women's Club Volleyball
mission: The purpose of Women’s Club Volleyball is to unite women from UW-Madison together to play at a highly competitive level against universities across the country. The Club consists of three traveling teams, one with a lesser time commitment than the other two. Our members will experience a high level of play that allows them to continue their volleyball careers with a commitment that gives members the ability to be involved in other activities around campus. To make club volleyball an affordable option for all members, we have many fundraising events that provide great support for our club. Beyond volleyball, our organization fosters great friendships that could last a lifetime. These women will bond over their love of the sport while experiencing support and encouragement that comes from being a part of something larger than oneself.

name: Women's Club Water Polo (UW-Madison)
mission: As a sports club, this organization was created to provide those interested in continuing water polo at the collegiate level with a safe and welcoming community where they could further their athletic pursuits while also forming friendships and growing leadership skills.
membershipBenefits: - Competing in typically one home tournament in the fall and four away tournaments in the spring, including the Big10 tournament where we get the opportunity to qualify for nationals. - Practices two to three times a week at Soderholm Family Aquatic Center. - Opportunity to expand skills such as leadership, marketing, and coaching. - A fun, welcoming, and competitive community of students with similar interests.

name: Women's Fastpitch Club Softball, University of Wisconsin-Madison
mission: The mission of the Women’s Fastpitch Club Softball team is to provide student-athletes with the opportunity to compete at a high level while fostering a supportive, inclusive, and team-oriented environment. The club is committed to promoting athletic excellence, leadership, sportsmanship, and personal growth while allowing members to balance their academic, athletic, and personal responsibilities.

name: Women's Ice Hockey Club-University of Wisconsin
mission: The mission of the Women’s Ice Hockey Club at UW-Madison is to provide an inclusive, supportive, and competitive environment where students of all skill levels can develop their hockey abilities, build lasting friendships, and grow as leaders both on and off the ice. The club is committed to promoting the sport of women’s hockey on the UW-Madison campus by fostering teamwork, sportsmanship, personal development, and a passion for the game while representing the University of Wisconsin with integrity, respect, and pride.

name: Women's Law Student Association
mission: The mission of WLSA is to provide a forum for discussion of women’s legal issues in society; networking opportunities; academic and personal support; and to address the concerns regarding women's legal issues at the University of Wisconsin Law School.

name: Women's Rugby Football Club (UW-Madison)
mission: Women’s Rugby Football Club (University of Wisconsin-Madison) plays a competitive fall season against various colleges in the Midwest and a spring season that has tournaments across the country that we attend. Between the two seasons, we have team fund raisers, training sessions, and other fun events. We strive to teach the game of rugby to interested women’s of all levels of experiences. We are a fun-loving group of girls and we want you to play rugby!

name: World Beyond War - UW Madison Chapter
WSB Leadership Lab
mission: Our Leadership Lab fosters opportunities for pre-business, certificate in business, and undergraduate business students to level up their leadership skills. Whether you are just starting your leadership journey or already applying leadership skills, our program offers intentional development for all our students. We at Wisconsin School of Business build leaders who are Trusted to Lead.

name: WSB Marketing Leadership Institute
mission: Connecting students to marketing industry professionals.

name: WSB Presenting and Writing Lab
mission: The Presenting and Writing Lab builds students’ confidence in professional communication through supportive one-on-one coaching. We offer students skill-driven advice designed to help them transition from academic communicators to successful workplace communicators. Our approach is student driven; we encourage students to analyze assignments, ask critical questions, and consider their work from the audience’s perspective. Our goal is for students to leave with concrete strategies for effective professional presenting and writing.

name: WUD Art Committee
mission: The Wisconsin Union Directorate Art Committee is dedicated to bringing novel and challenging exhibitions to the Wisconsin Union and advancing visual arts in the Madison community.

name: WUD Film Committee
mission: The Wisconsin Union Directorate Film Committee is a student-run organization dedicated to bringing a diverse, innovative, and exciting lineup of movies to the University of Wisconsin – Madison campus and surrounding community.

name: WUD Games Committee
mission: The mission of WUD Games is to provide a fun and welcoming environment through the use of games and the gaming community.

name: WUD Global Connections
mission: The Wisconsin Union Directorate Global Connections Committee is a fun and engaging organization open to any UW student. We strive to foster awareness of global issues and interests in various cultures and strive to close the understanding gap between people of different cultures and identities through our various programs. WUD Global Connections offers the opportunity to build long-lasting friendships and connections on campus (and beyond!), as we bridge the gap between domestic and international members of our campus community. The Global Connections Committee is open to all UW-Madison students, both domestic and international. Please join us and bring a friend! The committee meets weekly during the academic year, meeting day and times coming soon! Please check TITU for a specific room location.
membershipBenefits: By participating in Global Connections, you will not only get hands-on experience in event planning, but also have opportunities to network throughout campus. Come to a committee meeting or email us if you would like more information.

name: WUD Literary Arts Committee
mission: The Wisconsin Union Directorate Literary Arts Committee (WUD Lit) is dedicated to building community through the Literary Arts on the UW-Madison campus. We provide hands-on experience in publishing and in hosting events focused on engaging with the literary arts. We publish three student-run magazines—EMMIE, Illumination, and The Dish—highlighting the creativity of the UW-Madison community. Their content focuses on music, food journalism, and creative works of poetry, art, and prose

name: Young Democratic Socialists of America - UW-Madison
Zeta Beta Tau - Alpha Kappa Chapter
mission: The mission of Zeta Beta Tau's Alpha Kappa Chapter at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is to develop leaders of integrity through lifelong brotherhood, academic excellence, community service, and personal growth. We strive to foster an inclusive environment that empowers members to succeed professionally, academically, and socially while making a positive impact on the university and surrounding community.
membershipBenefits: Membership provides opportunities to build lasting friendships, develop leadership skills, participate in community service and philanthropy, grow professionally through networking and alumni connections, and engage in social and campus activities while contributing to the success of the chapter.

name: Zeta Tau Alpha - Lambda Upsilon Chapter
mission: The mission of Zeta Tau Alpha is to make a difference in the lives of our membership by developing the potential of each individual through innovative programming which emphasizes leadership development, service to others, academic achievement and continued personal growth for women, with a commitment to friendship and the future based on the sisterhood, values and traditions of the past.
membershipBenefits: Sisterhood, philanthropy and service opportunities, academic support, leadership experience, scholarship eligibility, professional and personal development, and a lifelong alumni network.
